A10:
CSR (Sec 135, Companies Act 2013)

  • Applies if net worth ≥ ₹500 cr, or turnover ≥ ₹1,000 cr, or net profit ≥ ₹5 cr.
  • Spend 2% of average net profit of the preceding 3 years. If the average is negative → nil.
  • CSR committee: 3 directors, at least 1 independent.
  • Non-compliance is a civil wrong (2021): penalty twice the unspent amount, capped at ₹1 crore (company); 1/10th, capped at ₹2 lakh (officer).
  • Spending that only benefits the company or its employees is not CSR.

SDGs

17 goals, 169 targets, adopted by the UNGA in Sept 2015, in force 2016–2030; replaced the MDGs. SDG 13 = Climate Action; 14 = Life below Water; 15 = Life on Land. India coordinator: NITI Aayog.

Climate

  • Panchamrit (COP-26): 500 GW non-fossil capacity, 50% of energy from renewables, −1 bn t emissions, −45% carbon intensity (all by 2030); net zero by 2070.
  • OSOWOG = One Sun One World One Grid (global solar grid). Plastic Hackathon target: free of single-use plastic by 2022.
  • RBI: Sustainable Finance Group (DoR, 2021); green deposit framework (excludes fossil fuels); green bonds.
  • ESG: investors screen on environmental, social and governance criteria; governance serves all stakeholders, long term.

B2:
• Law of demand: price ↑ → quantity demanded ↓ (ceteris paribus) because of the substitution + income effects. The demand curve slopes downward. A demand schedule is a table of price vs quantity.
  • Exceptions: Giffen (inferior staples), Veblen (conspicuous consumption, status), expectations.
  • Determinants: own price, income, related-goods prices, tastes, population.
  • Movement along the curve = own-price change. Shift = non-price factors.
  • Diminishing marginal utility: each extra unit gives less extra satisfaction.
  • Supply curve = price vs quantity producers offer. Supply shifts left → price ↑.
Equilibrium sum: Qd = Qs → 100 − 4P = 28 + 2P → P = 12, Q = 52.

Money measures

MeasureComposition
M0 (reserve/base money)Currency in circulation + bankers' deposits with RBI + other deposits with RBI
M1 (narrow)Currency with public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with RBI
M2M1 + post office savings deposits
M3 (broad)M1 + time deposits with banks
M4M3 + all post office deposits
  • Money multiplier = M3 ÷ M0 (Friedman & Schwartz). Velocity = Nominal GDP ÷ M3.
  • Sources of M3 = net bank credit to government + bank credit to commercial sector + net forex assets of banks + govt currency liabilities − net non-monetary liabilities.
  • Functions of money: medium of exchange, store of value, measure of value, standard of deferred payment.

Inflation

  • Demand-pull: rising aggregate demand (government spending, tax cuts, more money). Cost-push: rising costs of key inputs with no substitutes (oil, monsoon failure).
  • CPI (NSO) and WPI (DPIIT) are monthly. WPI weight: manufactured products ≈ 64% (highest). new CPI base year 2024 (Feb 2026).
  • GDP deflator = Nominal ÷ Real × 100 — covers all goods and services.

Currency

RBI issues all notes except ₹1; the Government issues ₹1 notes and all coins. Notes can be issued up to ₹10,000. ₹2000 notes were withdrawn in May 2023 (exchange ₹20,000 at a time) but remain legal tender. Demonetisation is done by the Central Government under the RBI Act.

Keynes' motives for holding money: Transactions (income), Precautionary (contingencies), Speculative (interest rate / bond-price expectations).

IS-LM (Hicks-Hansen synthesis): IS = goods-market equilibrium (I = S); LM = money-market equilibrium (from liquidity preference). Their intersection gives equilibrium income and interest. Fiscal changes shift IS; monetary changes shift LM.

Framework

  • Inflation target: 4% CPI-Combined ± 2%, set by the Government in consultation with RBI (Sec 45ZA). new retained to 31 March 2031.
  • MPC (Sec 45ZB): 6 members — Governor (chair, casting vote), Deputy Governor (monetary policy), one RBI officer + 3 government nominees. Silent period: 7 days before to 7 days after. Failure to meet the target (3 consecutive quarters) → report to Government (Sec 45ZN).
  • Bank Rate = discount rate. Reverse repo absorbs liquidity (with collateral). VRRR: auction-based absorption, rate above fixed reverse repo.
  • OMO: buy G-secs → inject liquidity; sell → absorb. Types: outright and repo.
  • LTRO and TLTRO: 1- and 3-year tenors. TLTRO 2.0: 50% to small/mid NBFCs & MFIs.
  • MCLR = marginal cost of funds + negative carry on CRR + operating cost + tenor premium; published for overnight, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y. EBLR (Oct 2019): repo, 3M or 6M T-bill (FBIL), or another FBIL benchmark.
  • Hawkish = tightening (less money, fight inflation). MCLR/BPLR are bank-level rates, not policy rates.
CRR → RBI Act 42; SLR → BR Act 24. MSF is ABOVE repo. RBI pays no interest on CRR.

  • Option: the right, not obligation. Call = right to buy; put = right to sell; the writer has the obligation. American = any time to expiry; European = on expiry only.
  • Swap = exchange of cash flows. FRA "a × b" = starts in a months, ends in b months (borrow 6 m starting 3 m from now → 3 × 9).
  • Open interest = outstanding contracts. CDS market makers: SCBs (not payment banks/RRBs), PDs, NBFCs, AIFIs.
  • Drawback: speculation. Benefits: risk transfer, price discovery, low cost.
D7:
• Factoring: assignment of receivables (short-term), with or without recourse. Non-recourse = factor bears the credit risk.
  • International: single factor (import factor steps in only on buyer default), two-factor, direct export/import factoring.
  • Forfaiting: discounting medium/long-term export bills, without recourse.
  • Bill rediscounting = double discounting.
  • TReDS (RBI-regulated): MSME sellers; buyers (corporates, PSUs, govt departments); financiers (banks, NBFC-factors, FIs); 2023 insurers as the 4th participant. Without recourse to the MSME. Seller upload = factoring; buyer upload = reverse factoring.
D8:
• Venture capital: long-term equity in early-stage, high-risk, high-return innovative firms, with management participation; no collateral, no guaranteed return.
  • Exit routes: IPO, promoter buy-back, strategic sale, liquidation.
  • Regulator: SEBI (VCF Regulations 1996 → AIF Regulations 2012, Category I). Minimum firm commitment ₹5 crore per scheme. Not allowed: real estate, NBFC business, gold financing.
  • Bhatt Committee (1988) — VC guidelines.

Operating leaseFinance lease
Short-term; lessor maintains and bears obsolescence; cost recovered from many lessees (aircraft, computers, servers)Full payout over asset life; lessee bears risks
  • Leveraged lease: the lessor borrows part of the price. Sale & lease-back: sell the asset, then lease it back.
  • Book view: leasing leaves the D/E ratio unchanged, so the lessee shows a better D/E than a borrower.
  • Hire purchase = contract of bailment: possession now, ownership on the last instalment; the seller can repossess on default; the hirer claims depreciation and interest. Only movable tangible goods (not goodwill). Instalment sale ≠ HP (ownership passes at once).
D10:
• CICs (RBI-regulated): TransUnion CIBIL (first), Equifax, Experian, CRIF High Mark. Score 300–900. Fees capped at ₹10,000 (membership) / ₹5,000 (annual). Aditya Puri Committee: all credit institutions to join all CICs.
  • CRAs (SEBI-registered): CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, India Ratings, Acuité, Brickwork, Infomerics. Moody's, S&P and Fitch are global agencies.
  • Scale: AAA highest safety · AA high · A adequate · BBB moderate · BB moderate risk · B high risk · C very high risk · D default.
D11:
• Structure: sponsor → trust/trustees → AMC (manages the portfolio; SEBI minimum net worth); a custodian holds the securities. Regulated by SEBI. UTI (1963) was set up by the Government to develop MFs; AMFI is the industry body.
  • Open-ended (any time) vs close-ended (fixed maturity) vs interval funds.
  • Categories: index fund (95% in the index); liquid (≤ 91 days); ELSS (3-year lock-in); FoF (95% in other funds); gilt (≥ 80% G-secs); floater (≥ 65% floating rate); multicap (≥ 65% equity across caps).
  • NAV: 4 decimals for debt/index, 2 for equity (book). Risk-o-meter: 6 levels. SIP (invest) / SWP (withdraw).

  • NPS (PFRDA): Tier I mandatory/pension, Tier II voluntary; PRAN 12 digits.

D14:
• Financial-market functions: price discovery (supply/demand, risk attitudes, volatility, information, mechanisms), liquidity, mobilising savings, lower transaction costs. No guaranteed returns. No physical location needed.
  • Interconnectedness: shocks spread globally. Downsides: volatility and contagion. Equities usually move opposite to bond yields.
  • CAGR = (End ÷ Start)^(1/n) − 1 → 10,000 to 12,100 in 2 years = 10%.
D15:
• REITs and InvITs are regulated by SEBI (2014) and must distribute ≥ 90% of net distributable cash flows.
  • REIT types: equity, mortgage, hybrid (mix); by property: residential, office, healthcare, retail… (the book treats "industrial" as the odd one out).
  • InvIT sectors: energy, transport/logistics, communications (towers, fibre).
